title: 王不是观众：五步抢到关键格
title_en: The King Is No Spectator: Five Moves to Win the Key Square
summary: 没有将军也没有立即吃子，先用王取得空间，再决定兵从哪一侧制造突破。
summary_en: No check, no immediate capture. First give the king space, then decide from which side the pawns break through.
topic: 王兵残局的对王与关键格
topic_en: Opposition and key squares in king-and-pawn endgames
introduction: 进入残局后，王从需要保护的对象变成最强的近战棋子。只会推兵的人，常常把本来能赢的局面推成和棋。
这道题的五步目标不是升变，而是先让白王取得更积极的位置，再用兵固定黑王的选择。你要学习的是残局中的先后次序。
introduction_en: In the endgame the king turns from something to protect into the strongest piece at close range. Players who only push pawns often push a winning position into a draw.
The five-move goal here is not promotion but first making the white king more active, then using the pawns to fix Black's choices. What you will learn is the order of play in the endgame.

culture.title: 对王是残局的语法
culture.content: 古典残局教材把双方王隔一格相对称为 opposition。它不是神秘定式，而是一种迫使对方先让路的节奏工具。理解对王后，很多王兵残局不再需要死记。

culture_en.title: Opposition is the grammar of the endgame
culture_en.content: Classical endgame manuals call it opposition when two kings face each other with one square between them. It is not a mystical pattern but a rhythm tool that forces the opponent to give way. Understanding opposition makes many king-and-pawn endgames need no memorizing.

challenge.title: 五步让王先进入战场
challenge.instruction: 前三步优先改善王的位置，后两步才推进兵。不要一开始就把兵推到无法回头的位置。
challenge.goal: 白方走五步，抢占关键格并建立双兵推进。

steps.note: 第一步正确：Kd3 让王向中心靠近。残局里，王的一个格子常比兵的一步更值钱。
第二步正确：Kd4 继续取得空间，迫使黑王向侧面让路。
第三步正确：Ke5 抢到关键格。白王现在能支持两枚兵，而黑王被挤到侧翼。
第四步正确：f4 在王的保护下推进。黑方必须决定用哪枚兵建立阻挡。
第五步正确：g4 建立并排双兵。白王位置领先，后续可以根据黑方交换选择制造通路兵。

challenge.success: 五步完成。白王先抢关键格，再让双兵前进；局面优势来自王的位置，而不是某一次吃子。
challenge.defaultAnswer: 如果先推兵，黑王会更容易站到兵前形成封锁。白王先走到 e5 后，两枚兵才有可靠支撑，黑方也更难同时阻挡两翼。

errors.f2f4: 立即 f4 太早。黑王还在中心，能迅速靠近兵前；先走 Kd3，把最强残局棋子带进来。
errors.g2g4: 立即 g4 同样暴露推进目标。兵不能后退，王却还能改善；优先走可逆、增益更大的王步。

challenge.genericError: 先问残局里哪枚棋子最需要改善。当前答案不是兵，而是仍然离关键格较远的白王。

quick.为什么先走王: 兵一旦推进不能后退，王步却能增加控制格并保留选择。先改善王，通常能让后续兵步更安全。
quick.什么是关键格: 关键格是王一旦占据，就能可靠支持兵继续前进的格子。这里 e5 同时帮助 f、g 两兵。
quick.为什么双兵一起走: 并排兵可以互相制造交换选择，王则从后方支持。单兵过早冲刺更容易被黑王封锁。

suggestions.label: 为什么两枚兵一起推进？

challenge_en.title: Five moves to bring the king into the fight first
challenge_en.instruction: Spend the first three moves improving the king's position; only the last two push pawns. Don't advance a pawn to a point of no return at the start.
challenge_en.goal: White moves five times, seizing key squares and building a two-pawn advance.

steps.note: First move correct: Kd3 brings the king toward the center. In the endgame, one king square is often worth more than a pawn move.
Second move correct: Kd4 keeps gaining space, forcing the black king to give way to the side.
Third move correct: Ke5 wins the key square. The white king can now support both pawns while the black king is pushed to the flank.
Fourth move correct: f4 advances under the king's protection. Black must decide which pawn will build the block.
Fifth move correct: g4 creates a pair of connected pawns. With the king ahead, White can later choose which side to break through.

challenge_en.success: Five moves complete. The white king seized the key square first, then the pawns advanced; the advantage comes from the king's position, not from any single capture.
challenge_en.defaultAnswer: If you push a pawn first, the black king finds it easier to step in front and blockade. After the white king reaches e5, both pawns have reliable support and Black can hardly cover both wings at once.

errors.f2f4: Immediate f4 is too early. The black king is still in the center and can rush in front of the pawn; play Kd3 first and bring the strongest endgame piece into the fight.
errors.g2g4: Immediate g4 exposes the target just the same. Pawns cannot move backward, but the king can still improve; prefer the reversible, higher-gain king move.

challenge_en.genericError: Ask which piece most needs improving in the endgame. The answer here is not a pawn but the white king, still far from the key squares.

quick.为什么先走王: Once a pawn advances it cannot retreat, while a king move gains control and keeps options open. Improving the king first usually makes the later pawn moves safer.
quick.什么是关键格: A key square is one that, once occupied by the king, reliably supports the pawns' advance. Here e5 helps both the f- and g-pawns.
quick.为什么双兵一起走: Connected pawns give each other exchange options, and the king supports them from behind. A lone pawn rushing ahead is more easily blocked by the black king.

suggestions.label: Why do the first three moves all use the king?

review.title: 先让王领先，再让兵兑现
steps: Kd3、Kd4 用王取得中心空间并迫使黑王让路。
Ke5 是整个计划的关键，王开始同时支持两枚兵。
f4、g4 在王的保护下建立并排双兵。
整个过程没有立即吃子，但胜率随着王的位置持续提高。
review.principle: 王兵残局先比较王的位置，再决定兵步；不可逆的兵步应该建立在王已经改善的基础上。

review_en.title: Let the king lead, then let the pawns cash in
steps: Kd3, Kd4 use the king to take central space and force the black king aside.
Ke5 is the key of the whole plan: the king now supports both pawns.
f4, g4 build connected pawns under the king's protection.
No immediate captures anywhere, yet the win rate keeps climbing with the king's position.
review_en.principle: In king-and-pawn endgames compare the kings first, then decide on pawn moves; irreversible pawn moves should wait until the king has already improved.
